scan_metadata.paper: Generative Predictive Control: Flow Matching Policies for Dynamic and Difficult-to-Demonstrate Tasks (Vince Kurtz, Joel Burdick; arXiv 2502.13406)
scan_metadata.scope_filter: Simulation training and headless evaluation of the shipped example tasks (pendulum, cart_pole, double_cart_pole, particle, pusht, walker, crane, humanoid); hardware and interactive viewing out of scope.
scan_metadata.filter_application: The filter is a scope description, not a path substring or title. It matches all eight examples/<task>.py and the library code they call; nothing outside that scope was selected. The README custom-robot path and the viewer-only functions were not selected.
scan_metadata.explanation: Static scan only: no repository code was run and nothing was imported or installed. Five tools in two modules are proposed. Every tool calls a function or method in the pinned gpc tree; one (gpc_rollout_policy_closed_loop) is the non-viewer code of gpc.testing.test_interactive extracted with its source attributed, so the coordinator should confirm it is in scope. The paper's Sec. VI-A comparison (average cost per step for GPC/GPC+/SPC/PPO over 100 randomized runs, warm starts vs inpainting) is not in the pinned commit; it exists only on the unmerged branches origin/rl and origin/evals and is deferred. Feasibility has not been measured. Heavy jobs are currently disabled, and every env constructor needs an offscreen OpenGL context.
scan_metadata.module_design_note: Modules group tools by workflow: gpc_training owns the tools built on gpc/training.py; gpc_inference owns the three tools that use a trained policy (gpc/policy.py, gpc/testing.py, gpc/sampling.py), whose usage the examples' test/sample branches document. This keeps assignments at two implementers and two verifiers on a memory-limited machine. A one-module-per-upstream-file split (gpc_policy, gpc_testing, gpc_sampling) is possible if the coordinator prefers it; tool names and source bindings stay the same.

tutorials.title: README
tutorials.description: Install, example usage (train/test), custom-robot instructions, citation.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documentation; confirms the public API (gpc.training.train, gpc.testing.test_interactive, gpc.envs.TrainingEnv) used by the selected tools. No separate operation.

tutorials.title: Pendulum swing-up example (train / test / sample)
tutorials.description: Trains a flow-matching policy for pendulum swing-up with gpc.training.train (PredictiveSampling 8 samples, 2 policy samples, 128 envs, 10 iterations); test opens an interactive viewer; sample bootstraps predictive sampling in hydrax's viewer.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Smallest shipped task (paper: 30 s training on an RTX 4070) and therefore the reference execution for gpc_train_policy; its train branch is the owning source section of that tool. Test/sample branches are viewer-bound (covered headless by cart_pole_example).

tutorials.title: Cart-pole swing-up example (train / test / sample)
tutorials.description: Trains a cart-pole flow-matching policy, then either runs it with warm starts in an interactive viewer (test) or uses it to bootstrap predictive sampling in hydrax's viewer (sample).
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Small task whose test and sample branches document both deployment modes (GPC with warm start, GPC+); owning source for the three inference tools, executed headless (viewer replaced by bounded headless calls).

candidates.task_and_io: Train a GPC flow-matching policy on one shipped example task (pendulum, cart_pole, double_cart_pole, particle, pusht, walker, crane, humanoid) with that example's settings, optionally reduced through the problem-size parameters train() exposes. Inputs: task name, output directory, overrides (num_iters, num_envs, num_epochs, batch_size, learning_rate, num_policy_samples, SPC num_samples/noise_level, episode_length, checkpoint_every, num_videos, strategy, exploration_noise_level). Outputs: saved Policy pickle (Policy.save, cloudpickle), periodic checkpoints log_dir/<timestamp>/policy_ckpt_<i>.pkl, TensorBoard event file, and per-iteration training curves (sim/policy_cost, sim/spc_cost, sim/policy_best_frac, fit/loss, sim/time, fit/time; training.py:487-497) = the quantities of the paper's Fig. 5 training curves.

candidates.reason: Core GPC operation (Algorithm 1: alternate SPC data generation and flow-matching fit). One public library call; the eight example train branches are duplicate demonstrations that differ only in settings, merged into one tool with a task preset.

candidates.task_and_io: Evaluate a saved (or freshly initialised) GPC policy headlessly on new random initial states of an example task: run gpc.training.simulate_episode vmapped over num_envs initial conditions with the policy-augmented SPC controller, advancing the simulation either with the first policy sample (strategy='policy', i.e. GPC with warm-start level 0) or with the SPC mean updated using the policy samples (strategy='best', policy-bootstrapped SPC). Inputs: task, policy pickle path, num_envs, seed, strategy, exploration_noise_level, SPC num_samples/noise_level, num_policy_samples, episode_length. Outputs: per-step and mean J_spc and J_policy, fraction of states where the policy produced the lowest-cost sample (reductions as in train's jit_simulate, training.py:363-381), observation/action-sequence arrays and optional state trajectories saved to an .npz.

calls: jax.vmap(simulate_episode, in_axes=(None, None, None, None, 0, None)) as in training.py:363-367

verification_source: tests/test_training.py::test_simulate (ParticleEnv(episode_length=13), PredictiveSampling(8, 0.1), num_policy_samples=8, untrained DenoisingMLP [32,32] + BatchNorm; asserts y (13,4), U (13,5,2), U_guess (13,5,2), J_spc (13,), J_policy (13,), states.t (13,), qpos (13,2))

the policy produced by the pendulum_example execution, evaluated with the pendulum preset at small num_envs; verifier compares wrapper output with a direct vmapped simulate_episode call on the same seed
candidates.reason: The only headless, repository-native closed-loop evaluation at the pinned commit; it is a public function with a test and gives the policy-vs-SPC comparison that train() logs, but on new seeds, saved policies/checkpoints and either deployment strategy.
notes: J_spc / J_policy are the lowest predicted rollout costs (sum over the planning-horizon rollout, training.py:88-96) among SPC samples and among policy samples at each visited state. They are NOT the paper's closed-loop average cost per time step (Fig. 3); that metric is deferred (see deferred items).
simulate_episode hard-codes warm_start_level = 0.0 (training.py:69); the warm-start level cannot be varied here.
num_policy_samples must be >= 1: the cost split costs[: -num_policy_samples] (training.py:89) breaks for 0, so an SPC-only baseline is not available through this function.
State trajectories are full mjx.Data per env and step (training.py:114, 121-123); memory grows with num_envs x episode_length; return them only on request.

Outputs: num_samples x planning_horizon x nu action sequences in physical units [u_min, u_max] (JSON/.npy).

candidates.task_and_io: Headless closed-loop GPC rollout: CPU MuJoCo simulation of an example task where the trained policy re-plans at every physics step from the current observation with warm-start level alpha and applies the first action (the computation of gpc.testing.test_interactive without the viewer). Inputs: task, policy pickle path, num_steps (replaces the viewer's is_running loop), warm_start_level (default 1.0), inference_timestep (example value), seed, optional initial qpos/qvel/mocap (default per example). Outputs: time series of qpos, qvel, ctrl, observations and per-step inference time (.npz + summary). Supports the paper's warm-start comparison of Fig. 4 (alpha = 0 vs alpha = 1) as trajectories; no cost metric.

candidates.task_and_io: GPC+ planning step from a given state: predictive sampling whose Gaussian samples are augmented with flow-matching policy samples (paper Sec. V-2), via gpc.sampling.BootstrappedPredictiveSampling.optimize. Inputs: task, policy pickle path, state (default MjData per example, or user qpos/qvel/mocap), num_samples, num_policy_samples, noise_level, warm_start_level, inference_timestep, num_randomizations, seed, number of optimize calls (default 1). Outputs: optimized action-sequence knots (params.mean), total cost of every rollout split into Gaussian samples (first num_samples) and policy samples (last num_policy_samples) as gpc/training.py:84-96 documents, best cost per group and whether a policy sample was best.

calls: BootstrappedPredictiveSampling(policy, env.get_obs, num_policy_samples=..., warm_start_level=..., inference_timestep=..., task=env.task, num_samples=..., noise_level=...[, num_randomizations=...])

feasibility.measured: Nothing was run by the scanner (JAX/MuJoCo imports are heavy jobs and are disabled). All figures below are upstream settings or scaling arguments, not measurements.
feasibility.machine_state_at_scan: 2026-10-12: HEAVY_JOBS_DISABLED present in mcp-build (since 2026-10-02). free -m: MemAvailable about 2544 MB of 7532 MB; nvidia-smi: 1868 MiB of 8188 MiB GPU memory in use. heavy.sh caps a job at min(2800, MemAvailable - 1500) MB, i.e. about 1 GB at scan time; a 2.5 GB reference run needs about 4 GB available.
feasibility.gl_prerequisite: TrainingEnv.__init__ always creates mujoco.Renderer(task.mj_model) (gpc/envs/base.py:33), so constructing ANY env (every tool) needs an OpenGL context, even with num_videos=0. Observed (no code run): DISPLAY=:0 and WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 (WSLg), Mesa libEGL.so.1/libGL.so.1 in ldconfig, no OSMesa library. The environment manager must confirm MUJOCO_GL=egl or the default glfw backend through WSLg works inside heavy.sh's systemd scope; tests/test_env.py::test_render (expects frames of shape (10, 3, 240, 320)) is the repository's smoke test for this.
feasibility.import_side_effect: import gpc sets XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.9 and overwrites XLA_FLAGS with '--xla_gpu_triton_gemm_any=true ' (gpc/__init__.py). Any other XLA flag must be set after importing gpc and before the first JAX computation.
memory_drivers: train / simulate_episode: rollouts per simulation step = (SPC num_samples + num_policy_samples) x num_randomizations x num_envs, each of planning-horizon length (training.py:294-310).

simulate_episode stacks, for every env and every step, the observation, U, U_guess and a full mjx.Data state (lax.scan outputs, training.py:114, 121-123): memory grows with num_envs x episode_length x sizeof(mjx.Data). This is the largest term for humanoid/walker/crane.
fit: (num_envs x episode_length // batch_size) x num_epochs gradient steps per iteration (training.py:161-162, 229-231): mostly time, not memory.
num_videos x episode frames rendered on the CPU (240x320 RGB per frame at video_fps).
Inference tools: num_samples (policy), num_samples + num_policy_samples rollouts (GPC+), num_steps of CPU MuJoCo (closed loop) - small.

recommended_reference_settings.pendulum_example (gpc_train_policy): pendulum preset with num_iters=2, num_envs=32 (upstream 10, 128); keep episode_length=200, SPC 8/0.1, num_policy_samples=2, num_epochs=10, batch_size=128; num_videos=2 is cheap if GL works, else 0 (record). If killed at the cap, num_envs=16.
recommended_reference_settings.training_tests: Run tests/test_training.py unchanged (test_simulate tiny; test_fit 1000 steps on 192 points; test_train particle 128 envs x 100 steps x 16 samples x 3 iters with num_videos=2). Run from a scratch working directory (the tests create _test_train/ and _test_policy/ relative to the cwd) so the repository is not modified. Test sizes cannot be reduced without editing the tests; if test_train exceeds the cap, record that and run the same calls through a driver with num_envs=32 as a labelled deviation.
recommended_reference_settings.cart_pole_example (gpc_inference): cart_pole preset train with num_iters=2, num_envs=16, num_epochs=10 (upstream 10, 128, 100) to obtain a policy; then Policy.apply with the test settings (dt 0.1, alpha 1.0), a headless closed loop of about 200 MuJoCo steps from the default MjData, and one BootstrappedPredictiveSampling.optimize call with the sample settings (2 policy + 1 Gaussian samples, noise 0.1).
recommended_reference_settings.other presets: particle: test_train sizes or num_envs=32. double_cart_pole, pusht, walker, crane, humanoid: no reference runs planned; at upstream sizes they are well beyond the cap (paper: 6-113 min of desktop GPU time; humanoid/pusht have 16k-20k rollouts per step). Any smoke test must use num_iters=1, num_envs of a few, small episode_length, and must be recorded as reduced. humanoid is the least likely to fit at any useful size.

prerequisites: hydrax from git tag v0.0.1 (pyproject.toml) provides the tasks (models, costs, planning horizons) and PredictiveSampling/MPPI; not present on this machine at scan time, so hydrax-side details (task planning horizons other than pendulum=5 and particle=5, Trajectory fields, PredictiveSampling update rule) must be confirmed after installation.
